name: secret-box
description: Claude can use a secret without seeing it: a masked box saves keys to the macOS Keychain or Windows Credential Manager (or .env) and gives Claude a placeholder, use_secret loads a stored item as a placeholder, every key a tool prints comes back as a placeholder, and committing .env is refused

backend.title: Where the box saves
backend.description: auto: the macOS Keychain on a Mac, Windows Credential Manager on Windows, the project .env elsewhere. keychain saves to that vault (service = the name, nothing written to .env; macOS and Windows only); dotenv writes the project .env as before

refuseUnmaskable.title: Refuse Keychain reads it can't hide
refuseUnmaskable.description: macOS and Windows: refuse a Bash command that reads the Keychain (or Credential Manager) in a way secret-box can't pin to one item or hide (a variable, sudo, dump-keychain, security -i, a value under 8 characters). Off, the command runs and only the detector scans its output

listPrefixes.title: Keychain services list_key_names may show
listPrefixes.description: macOS and Windows: service-name prefixes, separated by commas (myapp/,openai). list_key_names shows the names of Keychain or Credential Manager items whose service starts with one, beside the items secret-box saved. Empty: only those

keychainAccount.title: Keychain account
keychainAccount.description: The account the box saves Keychain (or Credential Manager) items under. Empty means your macOS user name ($USER), or on Windows your Windows user name (%USERNAME%)

secrets.title: Hide secrets
secrets.description: Hide vendor-shaped keys and high-entropy tokens

pii.title: Hide personal information
pii.description: Hide email addresses and public IP addresses

hideEmails.title: Hide emails
hideEmails.description: With pii on, also hide email addresses. Turn off to hide only IP addresses

redactPrivateIps.title: Hide private IP addresses
redactPrivateIps.description: With pii on, also hide private and reserved IP addresses recognized by the detector

restoreInToolInputs.title: Put real values back for tools
restoreInToolInputs.description: Swap a placeholder back for its real value before a tool runs, so commands and file writes keep working

restoreTools.title: Tools that get real values
restoreTools.description: Tools that run on this machine and may receive the real value behind a placeholder, separated by commas. Never list a tool that sends its input to another model or the network (Agent, WebFetch, WebSearch)

ownApproval.title: Approve calls with real values itself
ownApproval.description: When a call that got real values put back would need approval, decide it on the call as written, with placeholders, so no dialog or classifier sees a key: your permission rules first, then (see ownPrompt) an allow or secret-box's own prompt. In plan mode such a call is refused until the plan ends; in dontAsk mode Claude Code's own answer stands. Off, Claude Code asks about the call with the real values in it, as before

ownPrompt.title: Ask before each call that uses a key
ownPrompt.description: With ownApproval on: when your permission rules don't decide a call that uses a key, show secret-box's own Allow/Deny prompt (placeholders only). Off, such a call is allowed without asking, and auto mode's classifier skips the whole command, not only the key

notify.title: Say when something is hidden
notify.description: Show a count on the tool row and a toast on a prompt

minEntropy.title: Entropy floor (bits per character)
minEntropy.description: A mixed-case token above this floor is treated as a secret. Raise it to hide less

minLength.title: Length floor
minLength.description: The shortest token the entropy test looks at

contextMinEntropy.title: Entropy floor next to a key name
contextMinEntropy.description: The floor used when the token sits after API_KEY=, "token":, Bearer and the like

allow.title: Never hide these
allow.description: Exact strings to leave alone, separated by commas

allowEmails.title: Never hide these emails
allowEmails.description: Exact addresses, or a domain written as @example.com, separated by commas

allowPrefixes.title: Never hide tokens starting with
allowPrefixes.description: Extra id prefixes to treat as public, separated by commas (price_, prod_ and the other Stripe object ids are already public)

allowUrlHosts.title: Never hide URL paths on these hosts
allowUrlHosts.description: Hosts such as app.todoist.com or *.example.com, separated by commas. The path of a link on one of them is kept as written; its query string is still scanned. Never list a host that puts credentials in the path

denyPrefixes.title: Always test tokens starting with
denyPrefixes.description: Prefixes to put back under the entropy test even though they look like a public id, separated by commas
